intro.text: These lines come from well-known writers whose work is now in the public domain, plus a few proverbs.
intro.tip: Read each quotation once before you start – it makes typing it much easier.

steps.title: Shakespeare
text: All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players; they have their exits and their entrances.
We know what we are, but know not what we may be.
steps.instructions: From plays written over 400 years ago.

steps.title: Proverbs
text: Practice makes perfect. Little by little, the bird builds its nest. Many hands make light work.
Slow and steady wins the race. Every journey begins with a single step. Well begun is half done.
steps.instructions: Old sayings that are still true – especially about typing!
